first_postfreeze_judgment.evidence:
> The contour of MCL is not in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside proximal portion, C/W tear; the possibility of avulsion fracture of femoral condyle attachment of MCL .
> The contour of PCL and LCL appear to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> Interstitial increased signal intensity of iliotibial band, R/O grade 1-2 injury.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> Abnormal signal intensity is noted in proximal tibia and distal femur, which shows low signal intensity on T1WI and high signal intensity on T2WI, in favor of bone contusion; suspicious of subchondral fracture of posterior aspect of lateral tibial plateau.
> Wavy folded contour of medial menisucs with linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial and lateral  meniscus, without significant extending into the surface, R/O grade 2 intrasubstance signal, maybe due to degeneration.
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis; small Baker's cyst.
> Increased fat stranding over popliteal fossa
> Muscle edema over vastus lateralis muscle.
> Spur formation of patella and tendinosis of quadriceps tendon.

Impression: 
1. C/W tear of ACL.
2. C/W tear of MCL with suspicious of avulsion fracture of MCL.
3. Bone contusion of distal femur and proximal tibia and R/O subchondral fracture of lateral tibial platesu.
first_postfreeze_judgment.rationale: I retain uncertain and propose changing the current positive. The final report directly diagnoses femoral and tibial contusions, but suspected fracture sites also involve the femoral MCL attachment and lateral tibia. No site of the broadly described marrow injury is explicitly separated from both candidate fractures. The original positive retained the tibial fracture clause but did not preserve the femoral avulsion context in its quote. I do not infer that every contusion lies at a fracture; I preserve unresolved anatomical separation under the no-discrete-fracture-line criterion. My own quote is explicitly expanded from the femoral attachment clause through the impression so its anatomical reasoning can be checked; my original frozen quote and judgment remain unchanged.

original.evidence:
Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Pain; anterior and lateral knee pain for 4 days after fall during skiing, with clicking, locking, and buckling 
Comparison: [REDACTED].

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla extremity system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Anterior translation of the tibia in reference to the femur. Osseous contusions along the lateral femoral condyle terminal sulcus, posterior lateral tibial plateau and peripheral medial femoral condyle. No acute fracture. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate hemarthrosis. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Complete tear of the proximal to midsubstance ACL. 
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Grade 1 MCL sprain. 
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Grade 1 sprain of the fibular collateral ligament. 
Posterolateral corner structures: As above.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 17 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
Grade 1 strain of the proximal popliteus muscle. No muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle. Edema along the posterolateral subcutaneous tissues.

IMPRESSION:
Findings compatible with acute pivot shift injury, including:
    -Complete tear of the proximal to midsubstance ACL.
    -Osseous contusions along the lateral femoral condyle terminal sulcus, posterior lateral tibial plateau, and peripheral medial tibial plateau.
    -Grade 1 MCL sprain.
    -Grade 1 fibular collateral ligament sprain. Grade 1 strain of the popliteus muscle.
    -Moderate hemarthrosis.
